To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PDBu-induced contractility is mediated via RhoA/ ROCK activation and not by PKC.
RhoA/ ROCK compared with PKC is constitutively active and contractility by phorbol 13,12-dibutyrate in human internal anal smooth muscle cells is associated with RHO/ROCK activation, rather than PKC.
PDBu-induced contraction of human IAS SMMCs was attenuated by RhoA inhibitor and Rho kinase inhibitor, and not by PKC inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unknown status of RhoA and its downstream effector ROCK in the human Ias smooth muscle cells in the PDBu-stimulated state.
the role of PKC and the RhoA/rock pathway in the pathogenesis of IAS dysfunction and the potential for therapeutic modulation of this pathway in the treatment of IAS dysfunction.
the unknown status of RhoA and its effector ROCK in the PDBu-stimulated state in the IAS SMC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human IAS contractility is regulated by RhoA/ ROCK, and not PKC, in the basal state.
PDBu-induced contraction is associated with the translocation of RHOA/ROCK and that this process is independent of PKC activation in the human IASC.
PDBu-induced contractile response in human IAS S MCs is associated with the RhoA/ ROCK activation and that RhoA/ ROCK compared with PKCs are constitutively activated in these SMCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PDBu-induced contraction in human IAS SSMCs is associated with Rhoa/ROCK activation and not PKC activation.

RhoA/ ROCK compared with PKC in the human IAs SMCs are constitutively activated, and the contraction induced by PDBu, a PKC activator is associated with the RhoA/ ROCK activation rather than with the PKC activation.
the RhoA/ ROCK is a key signaling molecule in the PDBu-stimulated state in human IAS S MCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PDBu-induced contractility in human IAS smooth muscle cells is associated with R hoA/ROCK and not PKC activation.
RhoA/ ROCK activation rather than PKA is the main contributor to the contraction of the human internal anal SMCs.
PDBu causes RhoA/ ROCK II translocation to the cell membrane and contraction of human IAS smooth muscle cells.
